summary: ph-common 1.1.0 is a stub package that beacons installer host metadata to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and require time
details: The package ships a `postinstall` script (`node beacon.cjs`) and an `index.js` main that both invoke beacon.cjs on require. beacon.cjs collects installer-side identifiers — hostname, install path, cwd, Node version, and OS info — and POSTs them to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The destination is not a first-party or documented publisher domain. index.js provides no real functionality: it exports a Proxy of no-op functions, so the only runtime effect of installing or requiring the package is the beacon. The combination of a stub `Compatibility shim` package, dual install-time and import-time triggers, a bare-IP non-TLS destination, and collection of installer host metadata is a recon/dependency-confusion payload that discloses the installer's identity and environment to an attacker-controlled host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
